_comment: The Why bank. Recognition gives a rough transcript; QuestionMatcher scores it against each entry's keywords. `keywords` are the words that must mostly be present — pick nouns, not question words. `alternates` are whole phrasings that should also hit.
_rule: The owl must never invent an answer. Nothing here is generated at runtime: if nothing matches, it says the unknownQuestion line from phrases.json and asks the child to check with a grown-up.
_size: 129 questions, inside the brief's 100-200. Every canonical phrasing and every alternate is asserted to resolve to its own question, so a new entry that shadows an old one fails the build rather than quietly stealing its answers.
_singleWord: An entry whose keywords or alternates reduce to ONE content word matches on that word alone, wherever it appears. That is right for 'volcano' or 'hibernation' and wrong for 'colour' - keep single-word candidates to words that only ever mean this question.

questions.text: Why does the moon follow me?

questions.text: How do fish breathe under water?

questions.text: Why do I have a shadow?

questions.text: Why do my teeth fall out?
alternates: why did my tooth fall out
questions.answer: Your first teeth are small, made for a small mouth. As your face grows, bigger ones push up underneath, and the little ones wobble and make room.

questions.text: Why are owls awake at night?
alternates: why do owls stay up at night
questions.answer: Owls have enormous eyes for seeing in the dark and feathers so soft that they fly without a sound. The night is when the mice come out, so that is when owls go to work.

questions.text: Why does the sky go dark at night?
alternates: why is it dark at night
questions.answer: Our whole world is a giant ball that turns around and around. When your side of the ball turns away from the sun, the sunlight cannot reach you any more, and that is night.

questions.text: Where does the sun go at night?
alternates: what happens to the sun at night
does the sun go to sleep
questions.answer: It does not go anywhere. The world turns, so the sun slides out of sight below the edge of the ground, and while it is night here it is daytime for children on the other side.

questions.text: Why does the moon change shape?
alternates: why is the moon a different shape
why is the moon a circle sometimes
questions.answer: The moon is always round, like a ball. The sun only lights up one side of it, and as the moon travels around us we see more or less of that lit side, so it looks like it is growing and shrinking.

questions.text: Where do the stars go in the daytime?
alternates: where are the stars in the day
why cant i see stars in the daytime
why do stars disappear in the morning
questions.answer: They are still there, all day long. The sun is so bright that its light fills the whole sky, and the little star lights are simply too faint to see next to it.

questions.text: Why does the sky turn orange in the evening?
alternates: why does the sky go red at sunset
what makes the sky pink in the evening
questions.answer: Sunlight is all the colours mixed together. In the evening the light comes to us the long way through the air, which scatters the blues away and leaves the oranges and reds to reach your eyes.

alternates: is the sun bigger than the earth
why does the sun look small

questions.text: Why do we have summer and winter?
alternates: why is it hot in summer

questions.text: Why is it cold in winter?
alternates: why is it colder in the winter
questions.answer: In winter your half of the world leans away from the sun. Its light arrives slanted and spread thin, and the nights are long, so the ground has more time to lose its warmth than to gain it.

questions.text: Why is the grass wet in the morning?
alternates: why is there water on the grass
why is the grass damp in the morning

what makes onions sting your eyes

questions.text: Why does water bubble when it is hot?
alternates: what are the bubbles when water boils

questions.text: Why do we brush our teeth?
alternates: why do i have to brush my teeth
why do we clean our teeth

questions.text: Why do dogs wag their tails?
alternates: what does a wagging tail mean
why does a dog wag its tail
questions.answer: A tail is how a dog shows what it is feeling. A loose swinging wag usually means happy and friendly; a stiff fast one can mean the dog is excited or unsure, so it is worth looking at the rest of the dog too.

alternates: why does a cat have whiskers

questions.text: Why do cats sleep so much?
alternates: why do cats sleep all day
why is my cat always asleep
questions.answer: Cats are built for short bursts of hunting, which uses a lot of energy very quickly. Resting most of the day keeps them ready, so a cat may sleep sixteen hours and still be up at dawn.

questions.text: How do cats always land on their feet?

how do cats turn in the air
do cats always land on their feet

questions.text: Why do bats hang upside down?

alternates: why are elephant ears so big
why do elephants flap their ears

questions.text: How can ants carry such big things?

questions.text: Why do rabbits have long ears?

why do bunnies have big ears

questions.text: Why do bears sleep all winter?

why do we sweat when running

why do we shake in the cold

why does my skin go crinkly in the bath

what is the smell of flowers for

alternates: why can i see myself in a mirror

questions.text: Why can you see through glass?

questions.text: Why do trains run on rails?

questions.text: How does an umbrella keep you dry?
alternates: how do umbrellas keep rain off
questions.answer: Its cloth is woven so tightly, and coated so the water beads up, that the rain cannot get through. It runs down the curve instead and drips off the edge, well away from you.

questions.text: Why does a candle go out when you blow it?
alternates: how do you blow out a candle
why does blowing put out a flame
questions.answer: A flame needs hot gas from the melted wax to keep burning. Blowing sweeps that hot gas away and cools the wick below the temperature it needs, and the flame has nothing left to burn.

questions.text: Why does my shadow change size?
alternates: why is my shadow long sometimes
why does my shadow get bigger
